questions.q: Why was John Thornton alone in camp when he rescued Buck?
choices: He had frozen his feet, and his partners left him to get well
He had quarrelled with his partners and they had gone on without him
He was waiting there for the mail train to bring him a letter
He had come north alone to search for gold along the river
questions.evidence: When John Thornton froze his feet in the previous December

questions.q: How did Skeet, the little Irish setter, help Buck after his rescue?
choices: She brought him scraps of meat from the cooking fire
She washed and cleaned his wounds every morning
She kept the other dogs away while he slept by the river
She led him to a warm spot in the sun beside the tent
questions.evidence: so she washed and cleansed Buck's wounds

questions.q: What kind of dog was Nig?
choices: A small Irish setter with a gentle nature
A huge black half-bloodhound, half-deerhound
A grey husky who had pulled in the mail train
A spotted pointer brought up from the Southland
questions.evidence: a huge black dog, half bloodhound and half deerhound

questions.q: How was Buck's feeling for John Thornton different from his feeling for Judge Miller?
choices: He feared Thornton, but he had never once feared the Judge
It was passionate love, not just a dignified friendship
He obeyed Thornton only because Thornton fed him well
He liked the Judge much more but stayed with Thornton
questions.evidence: with the Judge himself, a stately and dignified friendship

questions.q: What made John Thornton "the ideal master" for his dogs?
choices: He cared for them as if they were his own children
He fed them more fish than any other man on the trail
He never made them pull a sled or carry a heavy pack
He trained them every day to obey his commands at once
questions.evidence: as if they were his own children

questions.q: What was Buck's special way of showing love that looked almost like hurting?
choices: He would jump hard against Thornton and knock him down
He would bite Thornton's hand in a pretend bite
He would growl and snarl whenever Thornton came near
He would pull Thornton's sleeve until the cloth tore
questions.evidence: this feigned bite for a caress

questions.q: Why did Buck get up in the night and listen at the tent flap to Thornton breathing?
choices: He heard wolves outside and wanted to warn his master
He was hungry and hoped Thornton would wake and feed him
He feared Thornton would leave his life like his other masters
He was guarding the camp against thieves from the river
questions.evidence: He was afraid that Thornton would pass out of his life

questions.q: Buck stole from other camps. Why did he never steal from John Thornton?
choices: Thornton kept all his food locked up in a strong box
Because of his very great love for Thornton
Thornton always gave him more than enough to eat
Skeet and Nig would have told on him right away
questions.evidence: Because of his very great love, he could not steal from this man

questions.q: What did Buck feel pulling at him from deep in the forest?
choices: The smell of a moose camp far across the hills
The howl of the wolf pack that hunted near Dawson
A call that lured him to turn his back on the fire
The sound of other dogs barking in a miners' camp
questions.evidence: Deep in the forest a call was sounding

questions.q: "After that he tolerated them in a passive sort of way." What does it mean that Buck "tolerated" Hans and Pete?
choices: He loved them as much as he loved Thornton
He put up with them but did not care for them
He was afraid of them and hid when they came
He fought with them every time they came near
questions.evidence: he tolerated them in a passive sort of way

questions.q: What happened when Thornton, on a whim, told Buck to jump off the cliff?
choices: Buck refused, lay down, and would not move from the spot
Buck sprang at once, and the men had to drag him back to safety
Buck barked at the edge until Thornton laughed and called him
Buck ran down a path to the bottom and waited there for them
questions.evidence: while Hans and Pete were dragging them back into safety

questions.q: What did the miners' meeting at Circle City decide after Buck attacked Black Burton?
choices: That Buck must be chained up and kept away from town
That the dog had good reason, so Buck was let go
That Thornton had to pay Burton for the harm done
That Buck had to be sold to a team leaving for Dawson
questions.evidence: decided that the dog had sufficient provocation

questions.q: Why did Buck attack Black Burton in the bar?
choices: Burton had tried to steal Buck from his corner
Burton had kicked Buck as he walked past him
Burton had struck John Thornton without warning
Burton had thrown his food on the floor at Buck
questions.evidence: Burton struck out, without warning, straight from the shoulder.

questions.q: How was Thornton thrown into the wild rapids of the Forty-Mile Creek?
choices: He slipped on a wet rock while walking along the bank
Hans checked the boat too suddenly and it flipped over
A tree fell across the boat as it passed a narrow bend
The rope broke and the boat was swept onto the rocks
questions.evidence: Hans checked it with the rope and checked too suddenly

questions.q: What did Buck do differently on his second try to reach Thornton in the river?
choices: He swam without the rope so that it could not pull him under
He swam straight out into the stream instead of at an angle
He waited for Hans to throw Thornton a long pole first
He swam up from below Thornton rather than coming down
questions.evidence: this time straight into the stream

questions.q: What injury did Thornton find on Buck after the river rescue?
choices: A badly cut front paw
Three of his ribs were broken
A deep gash on one shoulder
A sprained and swollen hind leg
questions.evidence: finding three broken ribs

questions.q: In the Eldorado Saloon, what did Thornton boast that Buck could do?
choices: Pull a loaded sled all the way from Dawson to Circle City
Start a sled with a thousand pounds and walk off with it
Beat any dog in Dawson in a fight in front of the crowd
Outrun the fastest dog team in Alaska over a mile
questions.evidence: Buck can start a thousand pounds.

questions.q: How did Thornton feel right after Matthewson slammed down his thousand dollars?
choices: Calm and sure, because he had seen Buck pull that much before
Doubtful and embarrassed, since he had no thousand dollars
Angry, because he thought Matthewson had cheated him
Excited, because he knew he would easily win the bet
questions.evidence: His tongue had tricked him.

questions.q: "The enormousness of it appalled him." What does "appalled" mean here?
choices: Pleased and delighted
Shocked and dismayed
Confused and puzzled
Bored and uninterested
questions.evidence: The enormousness of it appalled him.

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Buck's deep love for John Thornton and what he does for him
Buck becoming the leader of a new team of mail dogs
Thornton and his partners finding a rich vein of gold
Buck learning to hunt alone in the forest for his food
questions.evidence: Love, genuine passionate love, was his for the first time.
